intl_finance.notes: Penn does not issue the I-20 automatically: admitted students apply to ISSS through iPenn and upload financial documents and a passport copy; the admissions FAQ says to submit the I-20 application immediately upon accepting the offer of admission. No fixed date is published. Only the first academic year (fall and spring, summer excluded) must be covered; the total of the documents must equal or exceed the program's figure listed by ISSS. Accepted sources: your own savings or checking account, a pre-approved loan in your name, Penn-awarded funding, a non-Penn scholarship or grant, or a bank account in a parent's name (affidavit of support letter signed by that person). Documents must show bank name, account holder's full name, account type, date and final balance, must not be older than 1 year at the time of the I-20 application, and must be in English or translated; converting to US dollars is highly recommended. Investments are not accepted; investment or wealth portfolios, asset valuations, proof of employment or salary, and pension or retirement plans are not accepted. Official bank statement is recommended for the visa interview. Processing takes up to 3 weeks, no expedited processing. The CSS Profile and tax documents for financial aid are separate and are not this requirement.

Not acceptable: pay stubs, property deeds/titles, salary confirmations. Documents must be legible, in English, and not more than 6 months old at the time of admission.

deadlines.label: Financial documents for the I-20 (iStart)
deadlines.note: After admission and paying the enrollment deposit, W&M sends an iStart email; no fixed date is published.

intl_finance.notes: The estimate of funds used to issue the I-20 for Fall 2027 and Spring 2028 is $81,783 for a degree-seeking undergraduate (tuition and fees 56,211; living expenses 21,758; health insurance 3,814). W&M says it generally has no scholarships or loan funds for international undergraduates, so you must be able to fully finance your education. Scans are accepted, but bring the originals to the visa appointment. A new international student fee of $165 and a $85 per-semester service fee also apply.

william-mary.notes: The official checklist (source 2) says applicants are strongly encouraged to submit up to two of the 'optional essays' in the Common App, so college-specific essays exist and are optional. W&M's own pages do not print the prompt text or word limits, and the Common App W&M page could not be read, so no prompts are recorded and the 2026-27 wording is unconfirmed. Do not rely on third-party lists. Source 3 confirms the iStart step starts after admission and paying the enrollment deposit. The admissions international pages (applicationprocess, expensesaid) publish no financial document requirement; the I-20 funding rules above come from the ISSP office. Deadlines: Early Decision I November 1; Early Decision II and Regular Decision January 5.

prompts.prompt: Williams does not require a writing supplement, but we recognize that some students feel they do their best writing in an academic context rather than a personal narrative. If you would like to submit an example of your academic writing, you may share a 3- to 5-page paper (excluding citations) written in the last year. The paper may be creative or analytical, can cover any topic and need not be graded or include teacher comments. Please include a description of the assignment or prompt, and do not submit lab reports.

williams.notes: williams.edu blocks automated fetches, so this comes from the Internet Archive capture of the official first-year page dated 2026-06-24; the capture does not name the entry year, but it gives Regular Decision January 5 and Early Decision November 15.
